question_type: threshold count of investor categories holding a named security type (acronym 'TABs' = tax anticipation bills) on two Treasury Survey of Ownership dates, summed over two years
decisive_step: Reading 'Treasury TABs' literally as tax anticipation bills and therefore using the 'Tax anticipation:' sub-block of Section I Table 3 (Interest-Bearing Public Marketable Securities by Issues) in the March 1962 and March 1963 bulletins (the Jan-31 surveys), summing the TAB issues per grouped category (life+fire insurance, general+pension state/local), instead of the all-bills 'Treasury bills' row of Table 2 (Summary). The reference made this call at worklog.md Step 1 (lines 7-13) and located the rows at Step 3 (treasury_bulletin_1962_03.txt:3450-3452) and Step 4 (treasury_bulletin_1963_03.txt:3762-3763). A secondary trap is the 1963 Table 3 column order (USG+FR next-to-last, 'all other' last) which the reference pinned by matching Table 3's 'Total Treasury bills' row to Table 2's 'Treasury bills' row (worklog Step 4; review.md check 3).

a.path_summary: Found the Jan-31 surveys in the March 1962/1963 issues with find_tables (a[10]) and opened Table 2 Summary (a[13], a[15], a[20]). From the first THINK (a[4]) it treated 'TABs' as a probable typo for 'Treasury bills', took the all-bills row of Table 2 for both years, grouped insurance and state/local sub-columns into the 7 categories, ran printings on one cell (a[18]) and counted with calc (a[25]). A corpus grep for the literal acronym limited to the 1962-63 files came back empty (a[23]) and it took that as confirmation of the typo reading (a[24]). It never opened Table 3 (by issues), where the 'Tax anticipation:' sub-block lives.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Guessed at a[4] that TABs meant Treasury bills (or bonds) before seeing any table; at a[21] listed other expansions but never 'tax anticipation'; at a[23] grepped only the bare acronym in the two target-year files, got nothing, and at a[24] concluded the question meant the all-bills row. Counted categories on the Table 2 'Treasury bills' row, which puts most categories over the threshold in both years, so the count is several times the reference (>25pct).

notes: Two structural tool issues visible here. (1) TSO Table 3 headers are OCR-garbled in both years: 1962_03 show_table labels c7 as 'State and local governments > 487 corporations' (a[13], c[24]); 1963_03 Table 3 has one more header label than value columns (c[28]-c[30]) and 1963_03 Table 2 shows the USG+FR and 'all other' labels swapped (a[15]). show_table already emits a 'spurious extra label' note on other tables (seen in 038 c[26]); here it did not, and none of the cells got a label-independent anchor from the tool. A show_table note of the form 'header has 11 labels for 10 value columns; sibling table at :3717 has an identical row (Treasury bills = Total Treasury bills) with order ... ' would remove the trap that caught the v8 none arm. (2) printings keys rows by label, so for by-issue tables (row label = a security, e.g. 'Mar. 1963') it mixes surveys of different as-of dates (c[41]-c[44]); printings should print the as-of date per printing and let --as-of pin it. Also b's gate: recompute_final did not fire on a mentally computed count (no calc at all), the same gap pilot-1 noted.
